solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What Man Ray was, having a platform in outskirts of Detroit

indicators.note: the pieces sit in the middle of the outermost letters, enclosed by them
outskirts are the edges of a place, so only the end letters of the word are used

parts.note: a dais is a raised platform in a hall

explanation.surface: A photographer's biography noting he once had a stage on the edge of Detroit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' takes D and T from Detroit; A DAIS goes inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Man Ray, the American artist, was a leading figure of the Dada movement in Paris and New York.

clue.text: Racing yacht — something a female impersonator might have?

definitions.meaning: a class of keelboat raced in the Olympics

definitions.text: something a female impersonator might have?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., women's clothes worn by a drag artist

explanation.surface: Wondering what a drag queen might own.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word as DRAG ON: a female impersonator might well have drag on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dragon is a one-design racing keelboat; the split phrase describes wearing women's costume.

clue.text: Go with detectives, finding ruin

indicators.note: with signals the detectives going alongside the other piece, here in front

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
to repair to a place is to go there

explanation.surface: Accompanying the police on an investigation that ends in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are in answer order DIS + REPAIR; 'Go' is the formal 'repair to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A building in bad condition is in a state of decay, falling into ruin.

clue.text: First letter, one I penned in ancient language going north

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: penned in means enclosed, so the letter goes inside
in a down clue going north means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Latin is the ancient language of Rome

explanation.surface: Someone writes an initial letter in an old script, heading up the page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going north' turns LATIN into NITAL, and I goes inside it to give NITIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening letter of a name or word, as in signing with one's monogram, is this.

clue.text: Bored agent with woman in Thailand's borders

indicators.note: the agent and the woman are placed inside the border letters
the borders of a word are its outer letters

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A spy and a woman are bored stiff in Thailand's frontier zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' looks like weary but means drilled, as surgeons once drilled into skulls.
explanation.definitionFit: To trepan is to drill a hole in the skull with a surgical saw, so the past form means bored.

clue.text: A theatre award in New Mexico? It means the opposite

indicators.note: the award is placed within the state abbreviation, which surrounds it

parts.note: NM is the postal abbreviation for the US state of New Mexico
the Tony is the main Broadway theatre award

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a Broadway prize might be held in New Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the odd idea of the award being 'in' a state; it is literally written inside NM.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of contrary meaning, like hot for cold, is the opposite-sense term in grammar.

clue.text: Letter revealing a union problem after seven years?

parts.note: the seven-year itch is the supposed restlessness in a marriage after seven years

explanation.surface: A note revealing marital trouble after seven years together.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the spelt-out name of the eighth letter of the alphabet, H.

clue.text: Giant, one meeting a fairy queen

parts.note: a titan is a giant
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A giant encounters a queen of the fairies, as in a fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream has a queen of the fairies by this name, wife of Oberon.

clue.text: In action it resembles saltpetre

indicators.note: the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A chemistry note that something in use looks like saltpetre.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate, used in gunpowder, is known by both names, the second being the British spelling of niter.

clue.text: Part of sailing vessel popular in mother's time

indicators.note: the popular word goes inside the mother's word

parts.note: mama's, the possessive of mother, written MAMAS
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Sailing ships were in fashion in Mum's day.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'mother's' is read as MAMA'S with the apostrophe dropped, so the possessive supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal mast of a sailing ship, carrying the main sail, is a part of the vessel.

clue.text: Self-denying sailors can finally purchase books

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, so sailors
a can is a tin

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of the word purchase is used

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Thrifty sailors who at last get round to buying books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is not the verb but the container, TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains from pleasures such as drink is practising self-denial.

clue.text: All the players make nearly half the ice cream

indicators.note: just short of half the eleven-letter dessert name is kept, from its start

parts.note: ...-frutti is an ice cream with mixed candied fruit

explanation.surface: An instruction for an orchestra to cut a dessert nearly in two.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the eleven letters of TUTTI-FRUTTI, the first five, just under half, survive.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the Italian term marks a passage played by the whole ensemble together.

clue.text: Daggers produced by old boy and priest

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
Eli is the priest in the Bible who brought up Samuel

explanation.surface: Knives produced by a former pupil and a clergyman, like evidence in a murder case.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, these are the dagger-shaped marks used for footnotes, plural of obelus.

clue.text: At that time a group of nations invested in American club

indicators.note: to be invested in is to be put inside, here within the abbreviation

parts.note: at that time means then
the EU, European Union, is a group of nations

explanation.surface: Talk of an international bloc once pouring money into an American society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' reads as finance but means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenaeum is a famous London gentlemen's club, and the word names literary or scientific clubs generally.

clue.text: Jurassic creature's talons oddly displayed in a house

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'has', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the jumbled claws go inside the zodiac house

parts.note: Taurus is one of the twelve astrological houses or signs

indicators.note: the letters are shown in a strange order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dinosaur's claws are strangely exhibited inside a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tempts you to take odd letters, but with 'displayed' it signals an anagram; 'house' is an astrological house, a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large sauropod dinosaur known from fossils of the Jurassic period in North America.

clue.text: Old, old city's little people — us, emphatically

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia; the 's adds S
elves are the little people of folklore

explanation.surface: Our heritage from an ancient city and its folklore figures, stressed.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun is used for emphasis, as in 'we did it by our own hands'.

clue.text: Scallywags generally in right order crossing a burn?

indicators.note: the outer pieces stretch across the burn, enclosing it

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
to scald is to burn with hot liquid

explanation.surface: Rogues all in the correct sequence walking over a Scottish stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burn' suggests the Scottish word for a stream but is the verb for injuring with heat; 'crossing' puts the right-and-order pair on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -dom names a collective, so the word means rogues as a class.

clue.text: Eccentric leader leaving NW town for a Welsh one

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person

indicators.note: the first letter of the town departs

parts.note: Wigan is a town in north-west England

explanation.surface: An oddball boss moves from Wigan to a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Wigan is a town in Lancashire in north-west England; 'one' means a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardigan is a town on the west coast of Wales, so it is a Welsh town.

clue.text: Affected elegance of melodies with decorations

parts.note: airs are tunes
and means with, as in adding together
graces are musical ornaments, grace notes

explanation.surface: A musical description of tunes and ornamentation that sounds like a pretentious style.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on airs means behaving with a pretended refinement to impress others.

clue.text: Stuffy, like follicularly challenged Cockneys?

indicators.note: Londoners of the East End drop the opening H in speech

parts.note: a jokey way of saying bald

explanation.surface: A teasing remark comparing a stuffy room to bald Londoners.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney, a working-class Londoner, traditionally drops initial H, so bald becomes 'AIRLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A room lacking fresh ventilation is close and stuffy.

clue.text: Church cheers fellow visiting, one giving out notes

indicators.note: a visitor comes inside, so the fellow goes within the other pieces

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
ta is British slang for thanks
Les is a man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: A church thanks a visiting man who hands out leaflets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving out notes' suggests a cashier but means producing musical sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument with hammers striking metal plates produces bell-like musical sounds.

clue.text: Hungarian publication unknown artist set up

parts.note: mag is short for magazine
algebra uses Y for an unknown

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means placed upwards, read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A magazine from Hungary established by an anonymous painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magyars are the dominant ethnic group of Hungary, and the word is used for the people and language.

clue.text: Attractive English teacher dips into trifle half-heartedly

indicators.note: the pieces go into the middle of the shortened word
the doubled letter at its heart is halved, keeping just one

parts.note: to dabble is to trifle with something
Sir is how British pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: A charming English master dips his spoon into a pudding without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' looks like the British pudding but is the verb DABBLE, which loses one of its two Bs to make DABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth wanting is appealing, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Originally such a strange Wiltshire diocese

indicators.note: originally means taking the starting letters of the words

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd

explanation.surface: A remark that a diocese in Wiltshire is peculiar at its origins.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarum is the old name for Salisbury, whose bishop signs Sarum, so it names that Wiltshire see.

clue.text: The cheek of some musicians!

definitions.meaning: the section of an orchestra playing trumpets and trombones

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the nerve of a band.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass means effrontery as in 'brass neck', and also the orchestra's metal wind section.

clue.text: US city entertaining male climber

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold or host, so the city surrounds the man

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: Los Angeles playing host to a man who climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A woody vine of tropical forests that climbs up trees is the plant meant here.

clue.text: Stuff oneself with something close to Cheddar?

definitions.meaning: to eat greedily, overfill on food
the famous ravine near the Somerset village of Cheddar, which gives its name to the cheese

explanation.surface: Overeating on cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar is a village in Somerset, England, beside a famous limestone ravine; the cheese is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To gobble greedily is a verb sense; a steep rocky ravine is the noun, as at Cheddar.

clue.text: When swimming, lady dives with due consideration

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman takes a careful plunge into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting deliberately and after careful thought is doing things in a considered manner.

clue.text: Fate sailors reversed, avoiding area by island

indicators.note: avoiding means the area abbreviation is left out
reversed means the word for sailors is read backwards

parts.note: seamen are sailors

explanation.surface: Seamen turned back by fate, steering clear of a region near an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns SEAMEN into NEMAES; 'avoiding' drops its A to give NEMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, so the word means inescapable downfall or doom.

clue.text: Faker cops finally decisively overcome

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of the word cops is used

parts.note: to hammer an opponent is to beat them soundly

explanation.surface: A con artist is at last thoroughly beaten by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: One who shams is a pretender or impostor, someone faking an illness or feeling.
